formats.key: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
effects: Sets the owner list of the new Safe to _owners and the confirmation threshold to _threshold.
Sets fallbackHandler as the fallback handler when it is not the zero address.
Delegate-calls `to` with `data`, so code at `to` runs inside the Safe with its storage and balances. It can enable modules, set guards or move funds.
When payment > 0, the Safe pays `payment` of paymentToken (native currency when the token is zero) to paymentReceiver, or to tx.origin when paymentReceiver is zero.
formats.shown: "Setup Safe" with the owners, threshold, fallback handler, payment and its token, payment receiver, and `data` decoded as a normal call to `to` under the label "Module".

findings.title: setup decodes `data` as a call to `to`, but the Safe delegate-calls `to` with it.
findings.evidence: ModuleManager.setupModules: `if (!execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, type(uint256).max)) revertWithError("GS000");`. Descriptor setup field: {"path":"data","label":"Module","format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to"}}
findings.fix: Change the label to "Setup delegate call (runs in Safe)" and add a field for `to` with that label. Do not let the nested descriptor present it as a plain call to `to`.

findings.title: setup labels the delegate-call payload "Module", but it is arbitrary setup code, not a module.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "label": "Module" on `data`. Safe.setup: `setupModules(to, data);` runs any code at `to`. It does not register a module.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "Setup call" and show `to` as "Setup contract" (addressName).

findings.title: setup has no field for `to`, the contract whose code runs in the Safe.
findings.evidence: Descriptor setup fields: _owners, _threshold, fallbackHandler, payment, paymentReceiver, data. `to` appears only as calleePath. ModuleManager.setupModules delegate-calls `to`.
findings.fix: Add {"path":"to","label":"Setup contract","format":"addressName","params":{"types":["contract"]}}.

findings.title: setup shows a zero payment receiver literally, but the code pays tx.origin then.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver;`. Descriptor field paymentReceiver has no senderAddress.
findings.fix: Add "senderAddress": "$.metadata.constants.addressAsNull" to the paymentReceiver params, or relabel it "Payment receiver (0 = tx sender)".

findings.title: setup is bound to the Safe singleton, where setup always reverts. Real calls go to proxies.
findings.evidence: Safe constructor: `threshold = 1;` and OwnerManager.setupOwners: `if (threshold > 0) revertWithError("GS200");`. The only deployment is 0xFf51…a44b, the singleton.
findings.fix: Bind to Safe proxies (a factory constraint on SafeProxyFactory) or make sure the factory descriptor resolves this one through its singleton parameter.

formats.key: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
effects: The executor's msg.value (native currency) goes from the signer to the Safe. The function is payable.
The Safe calls or delegate-calls `to` with `value` of its native currency and `data`, depending on `operation`.
With operation = 1, code at `to` runs inside the Safe with its storage and balances.

When gasPrice > 0, the Safe pays (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice in gasToken (native when zero, capped at tx.gasprice) to refundReceiver, or to tx.origin when it is zero. It pays even when the inner call fails.
The executor's own address counts as an approving owner signature (v = 1 without a prior approveHash). The Safe nonce increments.
formats.shown: "sign multisig operation" with the operation type, the Safe, the executor, the nested call decoded against `to`, base gas raw, gas price as a token amount, and the gas receiver. safeTxGas and signatures are hidden. `to`, `value` and @.value have no field.

findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows @.value, the native currency the signer sends.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction is `external payable`. The descriptor execTransaction fields contain no `@.value` path.
findings.fix: Add {"path":"@.value","label":"Value sent to Safe","format":"amount"}.

findings.title: execTransaction has no field for `value`, the Safe's native currency sent to `to`.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute: `call(txGas, to, value, ...)`. The descriptor passes `value` only as amountPath of the `data` calldata field. With empty data (a plain ETH transfer), or a nested descriptor that does not show @.value, the amount and recipient are not shown.
findings.fix: Add {"path":"value","label":"Amount","format":"amount"} and {"path":"to","label":"To","format":"addressName"}, both visible always.

findings.title: execTransaction decodes `data` as a call to `to`, but with operation 1 it runs in the Safe.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, ...) }`. Descriptor field `data`: {"format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"}}. The enum shows "Delegate Call", but the nested screen then describes a call that does not occur.
findings.fix: Label the operation field "Operation type (Delegate Call runs target code in Safe)". Do not present the nested calldata as a call when the operation is 1.

findings.title: execTransaction intent "sign multisig operation" does not say that the Safe executes a transaction now.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "intent": "sign multisig operation". Safe.execTransaction checks the threshold signatures and then runs `execute(...)` and `handlePayment(...)`.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Execute Safe transaction" and add an interpolatedIntent that names `to` and `value`.

findings.title: execTransaction hides safeTxGas, which bounds the gas refund the Safe pays.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction: `execute(..., gasPrice == 0 ? (gasleft() - 2500) : safeTxGas)` and `payment = handlePayment(gasUsed, baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken, refundReceiver)`. Descriptor: {"label":"Safe Tx Gas","path":"safeTxGas","visible":"never"}.
findings.fix: Make safeTxGas visible (raw, label "Max execution gas") so that the refund ceiling (safeTxGas + baseGas) * gasPrice can be read.

findings.title: execTransaction labels baseGas "Gas amount" and shows a per-gas price as a token amount. The refund total is unclear.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice)`. Descriptor: baseGas "Gas amount" (raw), gasPrice "Gas price" (tokenAmount with gasToken).
findings.fix: Relabel baseGas "Base gas (refunded)" and gasPrice "Refund price per gas".

findings.title: execTransaction shows a zero refundReceiver literally, but the refund goes to tx.origin then.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver`. The descriptor refundReceiver field has no senderAddress.
findings.fix: Add "senderAddress": "$.metadata.constants.addressAsNull" to the refundReceiver params.

findings.title: execTransaction is bound to the Safe singleton, but signers send to their Safe proxy addresses.
findings.evidence: meta.json: proxyResolution.isProxy false, fullyQualifiedName contracts/Safe.sol:Safe at 0xff51…a44b. On the singleton, checkNSignatures reverts because `owners[currentOwner] == address(0)`.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies (a factory constraint on SafeProxyFactory ProxyCreation), not the singleton.

effects: Adds `owner` as an owner of the Safe.
Changes the confirmation threshold to _threshold when it differs from the current value.
formats.shown: "Add signer" with the new owner and the new threshold.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold restricts the new owner's address types to eoa, but contracts and Safes can be owners.
findings.evidence: Descriptor owner field: "types": ["eoa"]. OwnerManager.addOwnerWithThreshold rejects only the zero, sentinel and self addresses.
findings.fix: Set "types": ["eoa","wallet","contract"].

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold is self-only, and nested calls target the Safe proxy, not the bound singleton.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.addOwnerWithThreshold is `authorized`. SelfAuthorized: `if (msg.sender != address(this)) revertWithError("GS031");`. The deployment is the singleton 0xFf51…a44b.
findings.fix: Bind to Safe proxies so the nested lookup from execTransaction (callee = the Safe) resolves.

effects: Changes the threshold to _threshold when it differs from the current value.
formats.shown: "Remove signer" with the removed owner and the new threshold. prevOwner, a list pointer, is hidden.

findings.title: removeOwner restricts the removed owner's address types to eoa, but owners can be contracts.
findings.evidence: Descriptor owner field: "types": ["eoa"]. OwnerManager.setupOwners and addOwnerWithThreshold accept contract owners.
findings.fix: Set "types": ["eoa","wallet","contract"].

findings.title: removeOwner is self-only, and nested calls target the Safe proxy, not the bound singleton.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.removeOwner is `authorized`. The deployment is the singleton 0xFf51…a44b.
findings.fix: Bind to Safe proxies.

formats.key: swapOwner(address prevOwner, address oldOwner, address newOwner)
effects: Removes oldOwner and puts newOwner at its position as a Safe owner. The threshold does not change.
formats.shown: "Swap signer" with the old and new owner. prevOwner, a list pointer, is hidden.

findings.title: swapOwner restricts the old and new owner address types to eoa, but owners can be contracts.
findings.evidence: Descriptor oldOwner/newOwner: "types": ["eoa"]. OwnerManager.swapOwner rejects only zero, sentinel and self for newOwner.
findings.fix: Set "types": ["eoa","wallet","contract"] on both fields.

findings.title: swapOwner is self-only, and nested calls target the Safe proxy, not the bound singleton.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.swapOwner is `authorized`. The deployment is the singleton 0xFf51…a44b.
findings.fix: Bind to Safe proxies.

effects: Sets the number of owner confirmations that Safe transactions need to _threshold.

findings.title: changeThreshold is self-only, and nested calls target the Safe proxy, not the bound singleton.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.changeThreshold is `authorized`. The deployment is the singleton 0xFf51…a44b.
findings.fix: Bind to Safe proxies.

effects: Records hashToApprove as approved by the signer (an owner) for good. It counts as the signer's owner signature for any Safe transaction or message with that hash. There is no way to revoke it.
formats.shown: "Approve Safe hash" with the hash shown raw.

findings.title: approveHash shows only a hash, and the Safe transaction it approves cannot be decoded.
findings.evidence: Safe.approveHash: `approvedHashes[msg.sender][hashToApprove] = 1;`. checkNSignatures accepts it as an owner signature (v == 1). Descriptor field: hashToApprove raw.
findings.fix: None in ERC-7730. The wallet must show the Safe transaction behind the hash separately.

findings.title: approveHash intent does not say the approval is a permanent owner signature.
findings.evidence: meta.json devdoc approveHash: "The approved hash stays approved forever. There's no revocation mechanism". Descriptor intent: "Approve Safe hash".
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Sign Safe tx hash (permanent)".
